ledger.contains: BOI LTR visa brochure 2025 (2 pp.): launch date (1 Sep 2022), benefits (10-year renewable visa, re-entry, 1-year reporting, fast track, work permit, 17% tax for skilled professionals, overseas income exemption), four categories with 2025 criteria updates (Highly Skilled Professionals and industries, Work-from-Thailand, Wealthy Global Citizens, Wealthy Pensioners), dependants, insurance requirements, application steps (20 working days; visa within 60 days; 50,000 Baht fee), work permits, TIESC location and contacts. No statistics. Taken: all amounts and periods for the investor-linked categories (Wealthy Global Citizens; the Wealthy Pensioners investment option recorded with its own route), insurance, fees, validity, processing time and the 2025 rule change (the launch event was already in the data). Not taken (out of scope): income and employer thresholds of the Highly Skilled and Work-from-Thailand categories (not investment routes), the 17% tax rate.

BOI LTR visa website (stored 2026): TIESC (opened 17 March 2025), what the LTR visa is and the target of one million wealthy or talented residents in five years, privileges, four visa types with criteria (Highly Skilled, Work-from-Thailand, Wealthy Global Citizens, Wealthy Pensioners) and dependants, application process (20 working days endorsement, 1-3 days pre-approval, visa within 60 days, 50,000 Baht fee, work permit 3-5 days and 3,000 Baht a year), contact form, application channels (direct or VFS Global). No statistics on visas issued. Taken: the target, processing time and all amounts/periods for the investor-linked categories and dependants (investment, assets and visa fee already in the data). A commented-out line in the page source repeats an older US$80,000 income test for Wealthy Global Citizens; not taken (not displayed). Not taken (out of scope): income/employer thresholds and work-experience rules of the Highly Skilled and Work-from-Thailand categories.
